blinding_guess.why: The SET_DIGITAL_OUT, SET_FLAG, SET_ANALOG_OUT and SET_TOOL_VOLTAGE handlers each read socket_read_binary_integer(1+6+1), 8 integers copied from the SERVOJ handler, but use only one or two of them. notes: Unit is the URScript program snapshot:ur_driver/prog (installed by ur_driver/CMakeLists.txt:29). The ten elements are integer message-type IDs of a custom binary protocol over a raw TCP socket (socket_open(HOSTNAME, PORT), prog:144). They are not ROS messages, so there is no .msg/.srv definition and definition_id is null for every port. For the same reason the 'msg <pkg/Type>: <hash>' declares template cannot be filled without a placeholder. Each provided element is therefore recorded with the 'api' template on its verbatim constant declaration, which carries the wire ID. msg_type repeats the packet's canonical name for the message itself. QoS is null because this is ROS 1 and the transport is a plain socket, not a ROS topic. HOSTNAME and PORT are Python %-format placeholders (%(driver_hostname)s, %(driver_reverseport)d, prog:2-3) filled in at run time by whatever loads the program. frame is 'none' for all ports: the payloads are joint-space vectors, IO pin numbers and values, a payload mass, a time, a text string or an ID, and none of them carries a frame field. Physical units (rad, s, kg, V) are not stated in the code; units records only the fixed-point scale constants the code applies. Wire layouts at this revision. Sent by prog: MSG_OUT = int 1, then socket_send_string(msg), then socket_send_string("~") as terminator (prog:26-32). MSG_WAYPOINT_FINISHED = int 5, then int waypoint_id (prog:34-39); it is sent only after the MSG_MOVEJ branch (prog:200), and the call in the SERVOJ branch is commented out (prog:221). MSG_JOINT_STATES = int 3, then 18 ints (q[0..5], qdot[0..5], tau[0..5], each floor(10000.0*value)) (prog:48-66). In the same critical section and with no separate framing, it is followed by MSG_WRENCH (9) plus 6 ints floor(10000.0*tcp_force), and MSG_GET_IO (11) plus a digital-in bitmask (0-9), a digital-out bitmask (0-9), a flag bitmask built from pow(2,0)..pow(2,32) over flags 0-32, analog_out 0-1 and analog_in 0-3, each *1000000.0 (prog:67-83). The publisher loop sends once per sync() (prog:89-92); no numeric rate is set, so rate_hz is null. Read by prog after socket_read_binary_integer(1) gives the type (prog:166-173): SERVOJ reads 8 ints (id, q[6], t) and latches a setpoint for servoThread, which calls servoj(q, 0, 0, dt) (prog:202-222, 135). SET_PAYLOAD reads 1 int (prog:224). STOPJ reads nothing and calls stopj(1.0) (prog:233-235). SET_DIGITAL_OUT, SET_FLAG, SET_ANALOG_OUT and SET_TOOL_VOLTAGE each read 8 ints (1+6+1) and use params[1] (pin/voltage) and params[2] (value) only (prog:239-275). The digital-out and flag handlers treat value > 0 or != 0 as True. Other IDs declared but outside the packet: MSG_QUIT=2, MSG_MOVEJ=4, MSG_WRENCH=9, MSG_GET_IO=11. No exclusive resource claim is written in the code.
